title: The Role of Pipe Slope in Drainage Performance
description: Gravity is the primary driving force behind residential drainage systems, making correct pipe slope a critical factor in long-term performance. Maintaining a consistent downward fall ensures that both liquid waste and suspended solids move smoothly toward the main sewer line without stalling. If a drain pipe is installed with too little slope, wastewater slows down and solids can settle out, leading to recurring blockages. Conversely, if the slope is too steep, the liquid runs away too fast, leaving heavy waste behind stranded in the pipe. Professional installers rely on specified engineering guidelines and torpedo levels to achieve the correct fall for every specific pipe size and layout.
